review_notes: I read the whole file and checked every @[simp] declaration: fibreNormIndex_three/four, fibreNormMatrix_*, fibreSquareNormMatrix_*, fibreNorm_apply_two, fibreSquareNorm_apply, fibreSquareNormCoordinate_apply, mappingTorusProductCover_eq_productCover and surfacePeriodCoverCircleBoundary_apply. I grepped the library for their uses, including Core8 and PeriodFamily/Core7. Most are pointwise evaluations of private definitions at concrete constructors, with no cycle risk. The one questionable item is the simp attribute on the rfl-unfolding lemma for the circle-boundary map. This is a low-severity finding. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim about simp behaviour that was actually observed.

findings.excerpt:
surfacePeriodCoverCircleBoundary j p n a =
      PeriodTorusHigherHomology.circleBoundary (PeriodTorusHigherHomology.ProductTorus 3) n
findings.problem: This `rfl` lemma is tagged `@[simp]`. It unfolds the file's own named wrapper `surfacePeriodCoverCircleBoundary` into a composite of `circleBoundary` and `homeomorphHomologyEquiv`. That exposes the underlying Mathlib-style terms in any goal that mentions the wrapper. The wrapper exists so that statements such as `surfacePeriodCover_wangBoundary`, the `_secondMap` lemmas and `surfacePeriodCoverH4Coordinates_apply` can talk about one stable object. The Core8 consumers also use `surfacePeriodCoverCircleBoundary j p k b` in `change … at h` and `rw [h, fibreHomologyNorm…Coordinate_apply]` steps, where they expect it to stay folded. A later `simp` call on such goals would expand it and would no longer match the folded form those lemmas are stated in. The only external use found is an explicit `rw [Elliptic.HigherHomology.surfacePeriodCoverCircleBoundary_apply, …]` in PeriodFamily/Core7. This shows that the lemma is wanted as an opt-in rewrite and not as part of the default simp set. No use relies on it firing automatically.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `@[simp]` from `surfacePeriodCoverCircleBoundary_apply` and keep it as a plain `rfl` lemma used through `rw`/`simp [surfacePeriodCoverCircleBoundary_apply]`. Alternatively, mark the definition `@[irreducible]` and keep the lemma as the only unfolding interface. This keeps the simp normal form in terms of `surfacePeriodCoverCircleBoundary`. The same reasoning applies to `mappingTorusProductCover_eq_productCover` (line 412), which is also a `@[simp]` `rfl` unfolding that is only ever used by explicit `rw`.
findings.benefit: Default `simp` stops unfolding the wrapper into raw `circleBoundary ∘ homeomorphHomologyEquiv` terms. The downstream Core8 and PeriodFamily goals keep matching the `…Coordinate_apply` and `_secondMap` lemmas as stated. The simp set stays small, with no loss since all current uses are explicit `rw` calls.
